title: audit-log-exporter: wire up export sinks, retention policies, and installer hooks for Private
author: Aisha Raman
commits: Initial wiring: add helm chart values and configmap templates
Terraform module: add sink resources (s3/gcs/kafka) + retention and kms bindings
Installer hooks: post-install script to create sinks and bootstrap service accounts
Tests: add e2e test to validate sink plumbing and retention enforcement
Docs: document configuration knobs and example private values
description:
Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private require audit export and retention controls to satisfy compliance requirements (SOC2, ISO). This PR wires the audit-log-exporter into the Private installer and provisioning modules so operators can configure export sinks (S3/GCS/Kafka), retention windows, and KMS encryption keys as part of the normal install/upgrade flow. Changes include Helm chart updates, Terraform module bits, installer hooks, RBAC manifests, and an e2e test that validates sink creation and retention enforcement.

What this PR does: - Adds new values and templates in the Helm chart (audit-log-exporter) to configure multiple export sinks and per-sink retention. - Extends the Terraform module to provision sink resources when the customer chooses managed sinks: S3 bucket with lifecycle policy, GCS bucket with TTL, or Kafka topic + connector metadata. - Adds optional KMS key integration so exported logs can be encrypted with customer-managed keys. - Adds an installer post-install hook that sequences sink provisioning before the audit-log-exporter deployment and bootstraps service accounts and RBAC roles so the exporter can write to the sinks. Hook is idempotent and safe for upgrades/rollbacks. - Adds RBAC manifest to the rbac-policy-bundle for on-prem operators who prefer to apply bodies outside Helm. - Adds an e2e test that validates sink wiring, writes a sample audit event, and asserts the retention policy is applied (uses test-only helper to inspect bucket lifecycle and topic TTL). - Documentation: updates to README and example values for private installs.

Notes on config surface: - values.private.example.yaml exposes sinks: [s3, gcs, kafka], each with bucket/topic name, region, retention_days, kms_key_ref, and optional archive_policy. - Terraform variables allow choosing 'managed' or 'external' sinks; when managed, TF creates the bucket/topic and lifecycle rules. - Installer hook accepts a --dry-run and will defer to existing resources if external sink config is provided.

Security & compliance considerations: - KMS integration added to ensure customers can supply KMS/HSM keys for encryption-at-rest for exported logs. - RBAC roles are narrowly scoped: the exporter SA only has write permissions to configured sink resources. - Audit export retention is enforced at the sink resource level (bucket lifecycle / topic retention) rather than only inside the exporter to ensure defensibility.

Testing: - Unit: added template tests for Helm values and Terraform variable validation. - Integration: added test_audit_export_sinks.py which spins up a kube test namespace, applies installer with managed test sinks (minio for S3-compatible, local-gcs emulator) and validates that exported messages appear and retention rules exist.

CI: The first pipeline run hit a flaky e2e due to timing between hook and deployment; added retries and a readiness probe in the hook script. Final CI run: pass.

Migration/Upgrade path: - On upgrades the installer hook will detect existing buckets/topics and will not attempt to recreate them. - For customers with existing external sinks, set sinks.[name].external=true in values to skip provisioning. - Rollbacks: hooks are idempotent and include a safe cleanup step that only deletes test-created resources when a --cleanup flag is passed; default behavior is conservative (no destructive deletes).

Related: ENG-5123 (audit-export compliance), SEC-241 (kms + retention), SUP-1024 (customer request from support).

Checklist (completed): - [x] Helm values and templates added - [x] Terraform module for managed sinks - [x] Installer hook + idempotency - [x] KMS bindings + RBAC - [x] e2e test - [x] Docs and example values

Small migration notes for operators: - If you rely on external sinks, double-check values.private.example.yaml and set external=true to prevent accidental provisioning. - When opting into managed sinks, the installer will attempt to create lifecycle rules; ensure the installer principal has necessary cloud IAM permissions.

Merge: Squash merge to main after approvals.
